title: Insight 1: Easy ride pushed past easy threshold
description: On 2026-10-02 your average heart rate of 151bpm exceeded the easy zone (Z1 <139bpm) despite being labeled a recovery ride. Staying closer to 120bpm keeps effort comfortable while still building consistency. Try setting a cadence target to naturally limit intensity.

title: Insight 2: Long climb accumulates vertical strain
description: The 2026-09-26 ride covered 63.13km with 274m elevation gain and a 174W average power, showing your body responds well to hills but those climbs still tax legs. Even mostly flat-day riding contains small undulations—plan mixed-terrain days to spread the load.

title: Insight 3: Packed double-days risk incomplete recovery
description: October 1 and 6 both recorded cycling sessions within 48 hours, leaving limited time for full cardiovascular and muscular reset. Two back-to-back efforts like this can blunt long-term adaptations if intensity stays consistently high.

title: Insight 4: Distance growth outpaces daily consistency
description: Your October 1 ride (55km in 1h 46m) showed good distance addition compared to early September, but step counts dropped to 6,000 on October 6 with reduced sleep. Sustainable progress requires matching added miles to regular day-to-day movement.

title: Insight 5: FTP estimate needs fresh calibration
description: Your stored FTP of 271W from March 2025 conflicts with recent power outputs (peak 582W on Sept 26, 400-600W on other days). A modern testing protocol using your latest efforts will give accurate baseline for structuring workouts.

title: Insight 6: 80/20 polarized template fits your enjoyment
description: With recent mixes of sub-steady rides (~142-160W) and sprint bursts (up to 620W), an 80/20 split optimizes endurance base while preserving speed—most days stay below your aerobic threshold, saving energy for key sessions.

title: Insight 7: Watch for hidden fatigue signals
description: Lowest stress reading was 19 on October 6 paired with only 6h 49m sleep and decreasing readiness scores earlier in the week. Persistent downward trends in readiness indicate accumulated fatigue needing intentional rest.

title: Insight 8: Hammer hills build reactive power
description: The September 22 ride hit a peak of 514W during a 1-hour effort, proving you can sustain high power when motivated. Adding structured hill repeats (3-5 x 8min at max sustainable power) builds fast-twitch recruitment for climbing roads.

title: Insight 9: Intervals extend your aerobic ceiling
description: To broaden your cardio ceiling beyond current ~160-170bpm riding paces, try 5x4min intervals at 170-180bpm with 2min active recovery twice monthly. Consistent exposure improves VO2max more effectively than sporadic hard efforts.

title: Insight 10: Retrain your FTP with a functional test
description: Because your 2025 FTP estimate is outdated, perform a 20-minute functional test aiming for ~90% of 280W. Compare this result against recent sprint peaks (400-600W) to set realistic new baselines for all future workouts.
